The new commits fix the empty-slice panic in `average`, but they add a new panic in `first`.

- **Fixed:** `f-divide-by-zero`. `average` now returns 0 for an empty slice.
- **Not raised again:** `f-integer-division` was dropped earlier, so I left it alone.
- **New problem:** `first` panics when `n` is larger than the slice length. The neighbouring `last` clamps instead, so the two behave inconsistently. Neither function has tests.

draftedFindings.title: `first` panics when n > items.len()
draftedFindings.body: `&items[..n]` panics with an out-of-range slice index if `n` exceeds the length. The sibling `last` uses `saturating_sub` and never panics, so callers will reasonably expect `first` to clamp as well. Fix: `&items[..n.min(items.len())]`.
